items.title: Topical Questions
items.text: Teachers at Beckley Church of England primary school in my constituency, as well as parents of pupils, have contacted me to talk about the severe impact of the Government’s reforms of the way in which physical education is funded in schools on the school’s provision, in which there has been a massive drop. I am sure that that is not the intention of the reforms, but will the Minister agree to meet me to discuss what is happening in Beckley and at other schools?

items.title: Rosebank Oilfield
items.text: On Rosebank, the hon. Lady talks about the consequences of the climate heating. What percentage contribution will Rosebank make to the global warming of this country?

items.title: Rosebank Oilfield
items.text: Are we not at risk of swapping one set of vulnerabilities in relation to oil and gas and a country like Russia with another set of vulnerabilities in relation to a country like China, given its dominance of critical mineral supplies and solar panel manufacturing? We will be just as insecure, just in a different way.

items.title: UK-EU Relations
items.text: The Minister mentions Ukraine, which we have talked about today. Not having the arrangements with the EU that the Prime Minister is seeking in absolutely no way dampened our ability to work with Europe on Ukraine. We have been able to work together, and stand up strongly for Ukraine, under existing arrangements. What is so bad about them?

items.title: UK-EU Relations
items.text: I thank my hon. Friend for raising the point about how the EU behaves. I have such a strong sense of déjà vu. During the original negotiation period, every time that the EU was obstinate, stubborn and difficult, Labour Members sought to blame the Conservatives for that, instead of getting behind this country and standing up to that sort of behaviour.

docs.title: Application for a Premises Licence at Battle Abbey School Boarding House, Whatlington Road, Battle, TN33 0ND
docs.summary:
This report to the Rother District Council Licensing and General Purposes Committee, dated 16 November 2026, concerns a Premises Licence application for Battle Abbey School Boarding House, Whatlington Road, Battle, TN33 0ND. BAS (School) Limited seeks authorisation for the sale of alcohol and regulated entertainment, primarily for weddings and functions during school holidays. The officer recommendation is: "It be RESOLVED: That the application for a Premises Licence be determined."

The application was validated on 22 September 2026. Eight relevant representations objecting to the application were received, raising concerns about crime, public nuisance, safety, and child protection. Sussex Police raised no objection provided agreed conditions are attached. Rother DC Planning noted that the proposed use for weddings requires separate planning permission, distinct from the licensing regime. Environmental Health raised no concerns. The premises, formerly Leeford Lodge, previously held a licence surrendered in October 2024. The report notes one recent, unsubstantiated complaint regarding low-frequency noise. The Panel is tasked with determining the application in accordance with Section 18 of the Licensing Act 2003.

business.title: Performance Report: Second Quarter 2026/27

docs.title: Performance Report: Second Quarter 2026/27
docs.summary:
Rother District Council’s Overview and Scrutiny Committee met on 16 November 2026 to review the "Performance Report: Second Quarter 2026/27." The report, authored by Anna Evett, Head of Neighbourhood Services, monitors delivery of the Council’s Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) across nine service areas, including Housing, Climate Strategy, and Revenues.

Key findings include that net direct emissions rose 40% to 51.61 TCO2e, exceeding the target by 48.54 TCO2e. Income from assets is below target due to voids. Housing performance is described as "excellent," with an 80% increase in households prevented or relieved from homelessness compared to the previous quarter. However, the average cost of temporary accommodation is rising due to market supply and utility costs. Collection rates for Council Tax and Business Rates are currently challenging, prompting a focus on recovery and enforcement.

The officer recommendation states: "It be RESOLVED: That the Overview and Scrutiny Committee consider these findings and recommend any actions to Cabinet, as necessary." The report notes financial risks associated with rising temporary accommodation costs and asset income shortfalls. No legal, human rights, or GDPR implications were identified.

business.title: Budget Monitoring 2026/27, Revenue, Capital & Savings Targets Monitoring - Quarter 2 (Period 5) Update

docs.title: Budget Monitoring 2026/27, Revenue, Capital & Savings Targets Monitoring - Quarter 2 (Period 5) Update
docs.summary: Rother District Council’s Overview and Scrutiny Committee met on 16 November 2026 to review the 2026/27 budget. The report, prepared by Director of Resources Charlotte Spendly, forecasts a revenue surplus of £668,000, driven by favourable financing costs and savings in Waste Services, offset by deficits in Strategic Asset Management and Planning. The capital programme is forecast at £194.3m, with £41.0m spent in 2026/27. Key schemes include the De La Warr Pavilion, where works are delayed to March 2027, and Skinners Shed, which faces delays due to asbestos. The report notes that £477,700 of savings targets are deliverable, while £86,800 are undeliverable. The General Reserve is expected to increase to £3.392m. The officer recommendation was: “That the report be noted and the Committee makes any recommendations to Cabinet as necessary.” The meeting took place, and the document records the financial position for local residents and businesses affected by service changes and capital projects.

business.title: Housing Development Strategy Update

docs.title: Housing Development Strategy Update Report
docs.summary: This report to the Rother District Council Overview and Scrutiny Committee, dated 16 November 2026, updates members on the Housing Development Strategy adopted in July 2025. It recommends that Cabinet be requested to note progress, including the establishment of the Housing Delivery Team and support from the Council Housebuilding Support Service (CHoSS). The report proposes approving a programme feasibility budget of £192k under the Capital Programme for match funding, and approving a CHoSS revenue grant of £36,500 for feasibility work on five Council-owned sites. It also recommends granting delegated authority to the Director of Resources to receive grant awards. The strategy aims to deliver 557 new homes on Council-owned land, including 370 assumed temporary accommodation and social housing units, to reduce reliance on costly temporary accommodation currently costing £3.6 million annually. The wider Housing Development Programme targets 2,809 new dwellings by April 2029. These measures are intended to support homelessness priorities and provide a stronger case for external funding ahead of Local Government Reorganisation.

business.title: Performance Monitoring Report

docs.title: Performance Monitoring Report
docs.summary: This report to Rother District Council’s Shareholder Executive Committee on 18 November 2026 monitors the performance of Rother DC Housing Company (RDCHC) for the Blackfriars development. It recommends that “the latest cashflow (exempt appendix C) be used to update the Development Facility Agreement (DFA), and that the DFA itself is extended until 31 July 2029, to allow some scope for any further delays with the final completions expected in May 2029.” The report notes peak debt reached £38.6m in October 2026, with final completion of sales now expected by May 2029. Construction is progressing well, though a one-month delay impacted cashflow. The scheme aims to deliver 200 new dwellings, including 130 affordable homes. Councillor Coupar has resigned from the RDCHC Board, leaving four directors; the committee is asked to consider if a further RDC Member appointment is required. The report also highlights that the Tapestry scheme was shortlisted for a national development award.

business.title: Mitigations and Options Appraisal

docs.title: Mitigations and Options Appraisal
docs.summary:
Rother District Council’s Shareholder Executive Committee met on 18 November 2026 to review the financial position of its wholly owned housing company, Rother DC Housing Company (RDCHC). The report focuses on the “Tapestry” development in Battle, where 130 homes were pre-sold to Places for People, but 70 open market sale dwellings remain unsold due to weak market conditions.

The Council’s shareholder loan reached peak debt of £38.6m in October 2026 against a £40m facility. The report notes that while the company holds valuable assets, it faces cash flow constraints from ongoing interest and holding costs.

The committee recommended that “protecting the Council’s investment whilst maximising long-term value should remain the principal objective.” It further recommended that “a further report be provided to SEC in January 2027 with clear recommendations for progression once further analysis, due diligence and market testing has been completed.” The report assesses options including additional funding, loan restructuring, bulk sale, or conversion to long-term investment assets, noting that no single option is likely to deliver the optimum outcome in isolation.
